exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Volunteering Abroad
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: I've signed up to volunteer at a children's clinic in another country this summer.
Tom: That's brave of you, Mia. Aren't you worried about the language?
Mia: A little. But I think it's important to step outside my comfort zone.
Tom: True. What will you actually do there?
Mia: Mostly I'll assist the nurses and help teach families how to stay healthy.
Tom: That sounds really rewarding. How long will you stay?
Mia: About six weeks. It takes time to be truly useful to a team.
Tom: Well, I think it's a wonderful thing to do. Good luck!
exercises.translation_cn: 米娅报名暑假去另一个国家的儿童诊所做志愿者;汤姆担心语言问题;米娅觉得走出舒适区很重要;她主要协助护士、教家庭如何保持健康;要待大约六周,因为真正帮上团队需要时间;汤姆祝她好运。

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 Help Across Borders
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: An organisation called Doctors Without Borders was founded in Paris many years ago.
Its workers believe that medical care should cross every border.
They help people in danger, whatever country those people come from.
Those in the most serious danger are always treated first.
Today its members come from more than one hundred and fifty countries.

options: Medical care should cross every border.

questions.stem: Whom do they help?
options: People in danger from any country.

questions.stem: Who is treated first?

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Feeling at Home Abroad
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Ken: How was your first week living in London, Yuki?
Yuki: Honestly, the culture shock was bigger than I expected.
Ken: That's normal. Everything feels new at first.
Yuki: Yes. But my classmates were so welcoming that I soon felt better.
Ken: It helps to stay open and curious, doesn't it?
Yuki: Definitely. We share food from our home countries every Friday.
Ken: What a great idea! You learn from each other.
Yuki: Exactly. Now the world feels like one big village to me.
exercises.translation_cn: 肯问由纪在伦敦第一周怎么样;由纪坦言文化冲击比预想的大;肯说这很正常,起初一切都新鲜;由纪说同学很友好,她很快好起来;保持开放与好奇有帮助;他们每周五分享各自家乡的食物;互相学习;由纪觉得世界像一个大村庄。

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 A Speech That Mattered
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In 1863, a leader stood up in a field where many soldiers had died.
His speech lasted only about two minutes.
Yet his short words gave his divided people new hope.
He asked everyone to work towards the equality of all people.
Today that speech is still remembered as words that changed a nation.
exercises.translation_cn: 1863年,一位领袖站在许多士兵牺牲的战场上;他的演说只持续约两分钟;但简短的话语给分裂的人民带来新希望;他呼吁人人为所有人的平等而努力;如今这篇演说仍被铭记为改变了一个国家的话语。

options: In a field where soldiers had died.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Planning a Culture Day
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Let's plan our school's International Culture Day together.
Ben: Great. I think every class should present a different country.
Anna: Good idea. It is important to make every student feel included.
Ben: Right. We could invite families to share their own traditions too.
Anna: That would be wonderful. Food, music and dance from everywhere.
Ben: It takes real teamwork to organise such a big event.
Anna: True, but I'm sure it will be rewarding for the whole school.
Ben: Let's start sending out the invitations tomorrow.
exercises.translation_cn: 安娜提议一起筹划学校的国际文化日;本认为每个班级展示一个不同的国家;安娜说让每个学生都有参与感很重要;本建议邀请家庭来分享各自传统;来自各地的美食、音乐和舞蹈;本说办这么大的活动需要真正的团队协作;安娜相信对全校都很有意义;他们打算明天开始发邀请。

options: A class trip to the seaside.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 The Power of Sport
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sport has a special power to bring people together.
During a big match, fans from many countries cheer at the same moment.
Players shake hands and show respect, whoever wins the game.
People who share no common language can still enjoy the same goal.
In this way, sport helps to break down boundaries between strangers.
exercises.translation_cn: 体育有一种把人们聚到一起的特殊力量;一场大赛中,许多国家的球迷在同一刻欢呼;无论谁获胜,球员都握手致敬;没有共同语言的人也能一起为同一个进球喝彩;就这样,体育帮助打破陌生人之间的界限。

questions.stem: What special power does sport have?
options: It costs a lot of money.

questions.stem: What do fans from many countries do during a big match?
options: They cheer at the same moment.
